Compute pairwise weighted Cohen's kappa

Source: R/api-weighted-agreement.R
pairwise_kappa_table.Rd

Compare observed scores on matched units for every pair of raters, using quadratic (QWK), linear or unweighted agreement. No model is fitted.

Usage

pairwise_kappa_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  categories,
  weights = c("quadratic", "linear", "unweighted")
)

Arguments

data

Long-format ratings with at most one row per rater and unit.

rater

Name of the rater identifier column.

unit

Names of columns jointly identifying a rated unit, such as c("Person", "Task").

score

Name of the score column. Values may be numeric, character, factor or logical, with NA for missing scores. Factors use their labels.

categories

Required distinct permitted category values, including unused categories, in their substantive order. At least two are required. They must have the same numeric/character/logical representation as scores. With linear/quadratic weights, numeric values use their actual spacing; character/logical values use equally spaced positions in this vector. Factor levels never silently determine the order. To treat numeric codes as equally spaced ranks, explicitly convert scores and categories to character. Choose spacing on substantive grounds.

weights

One of "quadratic" (default), "linear" or "unweighted". Agreement weights are 1 minus squared normalized distance, 1 minus normalized absolute distance, or the identity matrix, respectively.

Value

A plain list with table (one row per pair), counts (nonzero retained contingency cells, with category indices), categories (indices, values and weighting positions), weights (agreement matrix), cases, units, settings and notes. Unit indexes units. Save with base::saveRDS() or export data frames with utils::write.csv().

Details

For each pair, both observed and expected agreement use only common complete units. Expected cell proportions are products of the two rater-specific margins on this same sample. Kappa is (observed - expected)/(1 - expected). This complete-case convention differs from the all-available rater margins in Gwet's incomplete-data Example 4.1. Different pairs may retain different cohorts; comparing or averaging their kappas does not establish a panel coefficient. At least two complete units are required, as in the existing QWK score-comparison interface.

Computation uses the equivalent disagreement ratio, with distances rescaled to the categories actually present in each retained pair. The common scale cancels, avoiding loss of the coefficient when an unused numeric category is very distant. ScaledObservedDisagreement and ScaledExpectedDisagreement retain those ingredients; agreement columns use the declared full-scale weights. Agreement columns can round to 1 at extreme relative spacings even when kappa is defined. Negative estimates remain visible; zero expected disagreement returns NA with a status.

Duplicate rater-unit cells are rejected before dropping missing scores. The case audit distinguishes an absent assignment from an explicit missing score and retains the union of units assigned to either member of the pair. No imputation, confidence intervals, tests or quality cutoffs are supplied. Missingness may affect representativeness. Agreement does not establish reference accuracy or MFRM rater-severity homogeneity. Storage of the weight matrix requires space quadratic in the number of declared categories; these are categorical-score interfaces, not continuous-score ICCs.

References

Cohen, J. (1968). Weighted kappa: nominal scale agreement with provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit. Psychological Bulletin, 70, 213-220. doi:10.1037/h0026256 .

Gwet, K. L. Handbook of Inter-Rater Reliability, fifth edition, volume 1, chapter 4, pp. 100-110, equations 4.2.4-4.2.6. https://www.agreestat.com/assets/cac5-chapter4-excerpt.pdf

See also

gwet_ac2_table(), krippendorff_alpha_table(), pairwise_icc_table(), score_comparison_table()

Examples

# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("pairwise_kappa_table", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
head(ratings) # One rater's score for one Person-Task response.
pairs <- pairwise_kappa_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", categories = 0:3)
pairs$table
pairs$cases # Included marks the shared nonmissing ratings for each pair.
# R2 gives every response one category more than R1: equal rankings do not
# imply agreement. Do not treat two Tasks by the same Person as one response.
} # }
